title: Telugu Student Anurup Reddy Drowns Saving Three Friends at Texas Reservoir
excerpt: The 22-year-old University of North Texas graduate rescued three friends from the Toledo Bend Reservoir spillway before a submerged fishing line trapped him underwater.
body:
• Anurup Reddy Koduru, 22, from Nalgonda district in Telangana, drowned at the Toledo Bend Reservoir spillway near the Texas-Louisiana border on May 29 after rescuing three friends from the water.
  • A recent Master's graduate in Computer Science from the University of North Texas, Koduru had just received a job offer worth approximately ₹1 crore annually.
  • His feet became entangled in a submerged fishing line after the rescue, and strong currents pulled him to a depth of 20 feet before emergency teams recovered his body.
  • His brother has launched a fundraiser to cover repatriation costs, and the Indian Consulate in Houston is assisting the family.

A 22-year-old Indian student from Telangana drowned at the Toledo Bend Reservoir on the Texas-Louisiana border on May 29 after successfully rescuing three friends who had slipped into the water while fishing. Anurup Reddy Koduru, a recent graduate of the University of North Texas in Denton, was on an outing to celebrate a friend's birthday when the incident occurred, according to multiple reports and a statement from the Sabine Parish Sheriff's Office.

How the rescue unfolded

Koduru was speaking on the phone near the reservoir's spillway when three of his friends, who were fishing nearby, lost their footing and were swept into the water by the current, according to family members cited by Hyderabad Mail. After another friend raised the alarm, Koduru — described as a strong swimmer — immediately jumped in and pulled all three to safety.

But while making his way back to shore, a discarded fishing line tangled around his legs. The strong underwater current at the spillway dragged him deeper, and despite his swimming ability, he could not free himself. Emergency responders from the Sabine Parish Sheriff's Dive Team, the Louisiana Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, and multiple regional fire and rescue agencies responded to the scene and recovered his body from a depth of approximately 20 feet.

"Sheriff Aaron Mitchell sadly reports a 22-year-old Denton, Texas man drowned this afternoon, Friday, May 29, 2026. Initial reports indicate the man was swimming with friends at the spillway near Toledo Bend Dam when he went under."

— Sabine Parish Sheriff’s Office statement

A promising career cut short

Koduru, originally from Shaligouraram mandal in Nalgonda district, had completed his engineering degree from Guru Nanak Engineering College in Hyderabad before moving to the United States for higher studies with his elder brother, Ashrith Reddy. During his third year of engineering, he had received a campus placement offer worth ₹40 lakh annually from a software company but turned it down to pursue a Master’s in Computer Science in the US, according to Hyderabad Mail.

He had recently completed his Master’s degree and received a job offer carrying an annual package of approximately ₹1 crore. Family members said he had not yet joined the company and was awaiting credentials related to the onboarding process when the tragedy struck.

Family’s grief and repatriation efforts

Koduru’s brother, Ashrit, launched a fundraising campaign to cover the costs of repatriating his body to India for last rites. The family, currently settled in Kavadipally village in Rangareddy district near Hyderabad, described themselves as "absolutely devastated."

"We are absolutely devastated, and our immediate priority is to transport his body from the United States back home to our parents and family in India. The cost of international repatriation, legal documentation, and transportation is incredibly high."

— Koduru family statement

The Indian Consulate in Houston posted condolences on social media and confirmed it was in contact with the family to provide assistance, according to Madhyamam Online. Koduru’s body was expected to arrive at Rajiv Gandhi International Airport in Hyderabad, after which last rites were to be conducted at the family’s residence.

A recurring pattern

Koduru’s death adds to a distressing series of fatalities involving Indian students in the United States, many of them from the Telugu-speaking states of Telangana and Andhra Pradesh. Drowning incidents at reservoirs, lakes, and rivers — where hidden hazards such as submerged fishing lines, sudden drop-offs, and strong currents are common — have been a recurring cause of death among young Indian nationals abroad.

Safety advocates have long urged recreational swimmers to exercise caution at unfamiliar water bodies, particularly near spillways and dam structures where underwater conditions can change rapidly. Toledo Bend Reservoir, the largest man-made body of water in the southern United States, is a popular fishing and recreation destination but has recorded multiple drowning incidents over the years.
